basic_info.name: Abridge
basic_info.description: Abridge is a commercial ambient-AI clinical documentation platform: its system listens to the live doctor-patient conversation, transcribes it, and drafts a structured clinical note (plus billing codes, referral letters and patient summaries) that the clinician reviews, edits and signs into the EHR. It was founded in 2018 and is the market leader in US ambient AI scribing, deeply integrated into Epic. The single most load-bearing fact is its scale and funding: Abridge reports deployment across more than 300 enterprise health systems representing over 250 million patients and supporting more than 100 million clinical conversations annually, backed by a ~$5.3B valuation. It is doctor-side and during-visit, designed to remove documentation burden - not a patient-facing pre-visit history-taking tool. In 2026 it expanded beyond documentation into an 'AI-native clinician intelligence platform' spanning pre-visit chart summaries, in-visit clinical decision support, coding and payer workflows.
basic_info.organization: Abridge AI, Inc. (commonly 'Abridge'), founded 2018 by Shivdev Rao (practicing cardiologist, CEO) and Sandeep Konam (CTO). Headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania with a major presence in San Francisco, California.

technical_features.what_it_does: Ambient clinical documentation: Abridge captures the audio of a clinician-patient encounter, performs proprietary automatic speech recognition, and generates a draft clinical note (e.g. H&P, progress note, consult note, specialty-specific notes) that the clinician reviews via a 'Linked Evidence' trace back to the transcript, edits and signs into the EHR. Beyond the note it produces billing/coding specificity, referral letters, handoff summaries and patient-facing summaries, and in 2026 it added pre-visit chart synthesis (a concise pre-visit brief/pre-drafted HPI and pre-round notes drawn from the longitudinal chart), in-visit context-aware clinical decision support, and evidence-grounded question answering. It does not conduct a patient-driven history interview; the content it summarizes is the live encounter and the existing chart, and the physician remains the author/attester.
technical_features.architecture: Cloud-based, enterprise SaaS built on an EHR-facing integration layer. Core components: a purpose-built automatic speech recognition system, a 'Contextual Reasoning Engine'/note-generation model pipeline, and a task-specific unsupported-claim (confabulation) detection-and-correction guardrail model trained on 50,000+ curated examples. In June 2026 Abridge announced a domain-adapted clinical foundation model co-developed with NVIDIA on the Nemotron open model family, trained on de-identified clinical data in pre/mid/post-training runs on NVIDIA Blackwell infrastructure, for data provenance and auditability. Integration with EHRs uses FHIR APIs (e.g. Epic), SMART-on-FHIR/OAuth and App Orchard/Partners-and-Pals channels, with notes written back as documents; there is no public developer API, sandbox or self-serve access.
technical_features.inputs: Ambient audio of the live clinician-patient conversation; prior chart context pulled from the EHR (demographics, problem list, medications, allergies, prior notes/labs/imaging); clinician-selected note type and smart-phrases; for pre-visit summaries, longitudinal chart data from prior encounters across care settings.
technical_features.outputs: Draft clinical documentation in the EHR (History & Physical, progress, consult and specialty notes), structured outputs such as discrete flowsheets, billing/ICD-style coding evidence, pharmacy orders, referral letters, handoff summaries, patient summaries, and pre-visit/pre-round summaries. Output is written to the EHR as documents (e.g. via FHIR DocumentReference) and requires clinician review and electronic signature; it is not an NRCeS/ABDM Composition or an HL7 IPS document.
technical_features.standards_compliance: Abridge integrates with US EHRs via FHIR APIs and SMART-on-FHIR OAuth (notably Epic's App Orchard / Partners and Pals and Epic Workshop), and is reported to conform to HIPAA plus SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and sign BAAs; it partners with AHIMA to audit its automated coding and CDI models. Its conformance claims are vendor- or partner-reported rather than validated against a public profile registry. It does not conform to the NRCeS FHIR IG for ABDM, the OPConsultRecord Composition profile, HL7 International Patient Summary, or India-specific terminologies (SNOMED CT India/CDCI/NAMASTE). No FHIR Composition/Bundle clinical-summary output contract is published; note exchange is through the host EHR rather than a standards-published summary profile.
technical_features.offline_capability: [uncertain] Abridge is a cloud platform: audio is streamed to Abridge Cloud and transcription, note generation and coding run server-side, so note generation requires connectivity. One third-party review states the mobile app can record an encounter offline in low-connectivity settings and sync later, but transcription/summarization still occur after reconnection; another notes the platform requires reliable internet. No first-party documentation of an offline or store-and-forward mode was found, so this is only partially supported single-source evidence.
technical_features.languages_supported: Abridge states its system is validated to capture encounters in 28+ languages across specialties and care settings, including Spanish, French, German, Italian, Chinese (Mandarin/Cantonese), Japanese, Haitian Creole, Arabic and Polish; non-English encounters are summarized into English notes. No evidence of Hindi, Devanagari-script rendering, or code-mixed Hinglish support, and notes are delivered in English rather than bilingual.
technical_features.deployment_model: Cloud SaaS, delivered inside the health system's existing enterprise deployment and security agreements. It runs embedded in the EHR (Abridge Inside, from Epic Haiku to Hyperdrive), via a companion mobile app and web experience connected to the patient chart, and on clinical workstations with a standard browser (Chrome/Edge). No on-premises or edge-inference requirement is published; all AI compute is cloud-side (NVIDIA Blackwell for training; provider-chosen inference). Implementation typically requires a multi-month IT procurement/integration cycle.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: Abridge's own published metrics: average note-quality 'star rating' of ~4.3 out of 5 across tens of thousands of clinician ratings (English encounters, a three-month window); a purpose-built confabulation detector that caught 97% of unsupported claims on an internal benchmark of 10,000+ encounters versus 82% for GPT-4o (i.e. an off-the-shelf model missed roughly six times as many confabulations); internal rubric-based offline evaluation where clinicians preferred an updated note agent in 91% of blinded comparisons (rule-checking LLM validated at 0.78 TPR / 0.07 FPR against clinician verdicts). Independent peer-reviewed ambient-AI evidence (not all Abridge-specific) shows the class is close to but slightly below physician notes on quality: a PDQI-9 study found ambient notes 4.20/5 vs physician 'gold' notes 4.25/5, with ambient more thorough/organized but less succinct and with hallucination present in 31% of ambient vs 20% of gold notes; a multi-country paired simulation found AI notes scored higher on PDQI-9 (40.6 vs 35.6) with fewer Critical+High errors than junior clinicians. Sutter Health's peer-reviewed studies (JAMA Netw Open, JAMIA) measure clinician wellbeing/experience rather than note accuracy.
performance_metrics.latency: Abridge's reference architecture and industry documentation describe note generation in roughly 10-30 seconds after the encounter closes, with real-time transcript fragments streamed during the visit. No first-party latency benchmark as a function of hardware or encounter length was found, and Abridge runs server-side so figures reflect cloud inference rather than on-device performance.
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: Not applicable to constrained edge hardware: all model inference runs in Abridge's cloud, so there is no published on-device RAM/VRAM/CPU footprint. Client devices need only a supported browser (Chrome/Edge) or the mobile app and reliable connectivity. Training uses NVIDIA Blackwell infrastructure. This is fundamentally different from a CPU-only kiosk requirement.
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: Deployed across more than 300 enterprise health systems representing over 250 million patients; more than 100 million clinical conversations annually (projected 2026); support for 28+ languages and 50+ specialties. Representative deployments: Sutter Health (unlimited enterprise access; 3,000+ users; five million notes generated as of July 2026); UCHealth (2,300+ of ~6,000 clinicians, Feb 2026); Geisinger (1,000+ clinicians in 10 months); Reid Health (nursing rollout, RN vacancy reportedly cut from 18% to ~8%). CDS monthly active users reportedly exceed 50% of eligible clinicians with per-clinician query volume tripling in two months (Aug 2026).
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: A layered, partly peer-reviewed protocol: (1) internal automated metrics during development (word error rate and medical-term recall for ASR; precision/recall of medical concepts between generated and human notes); (2) blinded clinician head-to-head comparisons with anytime-valid sequential hypothesis testing; (3) clinician-in-the-loop star ratings and edit-tracking in production; (4) rubric-based offline benchmarks across 20+ specialties with train/test splits and an LLM rule evaluator validated against clinician verdicts; (5) adversarial testing; and (6) external peer-reviewed studies by partner health systems (Sutter: JAMA Network Open May 2025, JAMIA April 2026). Caveat: several headline quality numbers are vendor-claimed/internal, and the most rigorous independent ambient-AI evaluations concern the product class rather than Abridge specifically.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: Abridge is the strongest available reference for what a credible clinical-summary quality bar and evaluation harness look like, even though its positioning is the opposite of MediKiosk (doctor-side, during-visit, cloud, English, US-EHR). It supplies three directly transferable things to Module C: (1) a defensible evaluation methodology - PDQI-9-style rubric scoring, concept recall, a clearly defined taxonomy of unsupported vs inferable vs unsupported-with-severity claims, adversarial testing, and blinded clinician head-to-head with train/test-separated internal benchmarks; (2) the provenance pattern that matters for physician trust and for MediKiosk's per-field provenance requirement - 'Linked Evidence' maps every generated statement back to its source (transcript/chart), which is exactly the transparency Module C needs for a patient-elicited summary; and (3) evidence that physicians will accept and edit AI-drafted notes only when they retain authorship/attestation - reinforcing MediKiosk's physician-attestation and elicit-never-diagnose design. It also shows that 'pre-visit summary' is now a real, funded product direction, but Abridge builds pre-visit briefs from the existing chart, not from new patient-elicited history - leaving Module C's elicitation-plus-digitization value unclaimed.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (1) the confabulation taxonomy (supported / inferable / unsupported, with severity grading) as the definition of hallucination for the Module C eval harness; (2) Linked Evidence-style per-claim provenance linking generated summary text back to the source utterance/document/field; (3) rubric-based offline benchmarks per specialty/Dashavidha-context with a held-out test split to prevent overfitting; (4) blinded clinician preference testing and star-ratings/edit-distance as ongoing real-world quality signals; (5) human-in-the-loop attestation as non-negotiable. Reject or heavily adapt: (1) cloud-only inference and connectivity assumptions (MediKiosk must run on a CPU/iGPU kiosk offline); (2) English-only note output and non-Indic language coverage (MediKiosk needs bilingual Hindi/Devanagari + English); (3) doctor-side during-visit capture (MediKiosk is patient-side pre-visit); (4) proprietary closed integration with no exportable summary contract; (5) any implied diagnostic/decision authority - Abridge's CDS outputs must not be mirrored into Module C, which must elicit and never diagnose.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: Abridge remains a cloud-dependent, English-output, US-EHR-centric product; it cannot run on a ~4GB CPU-only kiosk and has no offline or India-residency story. Hallucination is mitigated but not eliminated (independent class-level evidence found unsupported content in ~31% of ambient notes vs ~20% of clinician notes), and unaided clinician review detects only a minority of confirmed errors, so human oversight alone is not a complete safeguard. Note-quality findings are partly vendor-claimed, and some published quality studies concern ambient scribes generally or a different vendor rather than Abridge specifically. Its 2026 expansion into billing, payer adjudication, life sciences and CME raises scope, regulatory and conflict-of-interest questions. It offers no patient-elicited history capture, no document digitization, no ABDM/FHIR summary output, and no bilingual rendering - all core to Module C. There is also considerable hype/funding risk in the ambient-AI category (market shakeout, ~50x revenue multiple).
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: Abridge and MediKiosk sit on opposite sides of the encounter and address different problems, so Abridge does not directly compete with or erode MediKiosk's differentiation; it raises the quality and trust bar MediKiosk must meet. Abridge: doctor-side, during-visit capture, cloud inference, US EHR integration, English notes, proprietary output. MediKiosk: patient-side, pre-visit elicitation (voice + touch) plus digitized physical documents, offline-first on a CPU-only kiosk, India data residency, single bilingual physician-ready summary emitted against the NRCeS FHIR IG OPConsultRecord (Bundle.type=document), per-field provenance, elicit-never-diagnose, physician attestation. The overlap is methodological (evaluation, provenance, human-in-the-loop), not positional. The main threat is narrative: Abridge's 'pre-visit summaries' could be cited as evidence that pre-visit intelligence is already solved - MediKiosk must make clear that Abridge's pre-visit output is chart-derived, whereas Module C creates new structured history from the patient that did not previously exist in the record.

business_info.license: Proprietary commercial software; no open-source license. Private venture-backed company (Abridge AI, Inc.).
business_info.pricing: Not published; enterprise-only, quote-based contracts with no self-serve tier or free trial. Third-party estimates cluster around $2,500 per clinician per year (~$208/month) at entry, with full implementations reported at roughly $250-$800+ per provider per month and some estimates up to ~$1,200/provider/month or ~$2,500-$7,200+ per clinician per year, typically on 12-month minimums plus implementation costs. Figures are estimates, not vendor-confirmed.
business_info.funding: Approximately $830M raised across primary rounds (trackers range from ~$758M to ~$830M depending on what is counted). Reported sequence: $5M seed (2019); $10M Series A (2020); Series B (2023); $150M Series C at ~$850M valuation (Feb 2024); $250M Series D at $2.75B (Feb 2025); $300M Series E at $5.3B led by Andreessen Horowitz (Jun 2025); $316M Series E extension at the same $5.3B valuation (reported Apr 2026); and a corporate minority equity investment from Eli Lilly (Jun 2026). Investors include Andreessen Horowitz, Khosla Ventures, Bessemer Venture Partners, Lightspeed, Spark Capital, CVS Health Ventures, Kaiser Permanente Ventures, NVentures (NVIDIA) and the American College of Cardiology. Reported ARR ~$100M-$117M, implying a very high revenue multiple.
business_info.commercial_status: Commercial private company; enterprise SaaS sold directly to US health systems and payers. Market leader in ambient AI scribing (KLAS #1 Best in KLAS for Ambient AI in Revenue Cycle for 2025 and 2026) with a ~$5.3B reported valuation.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: US ambient documentation/AI-scribe: Microsoft Nuance DAX/Dragon Copilot, Ambience Healthcare, Suki AI, Nabla, Freed, Heidi (and Abridge's own broader platform now competes with coding/CDI and payer tools). Inpatient virtual-care/smart-room players (hellocare.ai, Artisight) and Epic's native ambient scribe are adjacent. India/ABDM comparators that also do documentation or patient-side digitization include Eka Care/EkaScribe, Sunoh.ai and Augnito Omni; none combines offline patient-elicited history with NRCeS OPConsultRecord emission, which remains the unoccupied space MediKiosk targets.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: Deep US EHR integration: Epic (first 'Pal' in Epic's Partners and Pals program, Epic Workshop participant; Abridge Inside from Haiku to Hyperdrive), plus Oracle Health/Cerner, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen and others via FHIR/SMART-on-FHIR. Content/knowledge partners include Wolters Kluwer UpToDate, NEJM, JAMA, ADA, AAFP and others; computing via NVIDIA; coding audit via AHIMA; payer engagement with Aetna, Cigna; smart-room integrations with hellocare.ai and Artisight. No ABDM gateway roles (HIP/HIU/PHR), no Health Locker, and no Indian HIS integrations.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: The ambient-AI scribe market is consolidating rapidly amid a structural shakeout, with Abridge, Microsoft/Nuance and Ambience as the leading funded players and Epic's native scribe embedded at no incremental license cost as a platform threat. Abridge is deliberately expanding from documentation into coding/revenue cycle, payer adjudication and life sciences, which increases both its strategic moat and its regulatory/conflict exposure. The category demonstrates strong procurement tailwinds for AI documentation in the US but no transferable India/ABDM pathway; Indian entrants remain cloud-first and app-based, leaving MediKiosk's offline, standards-conformant, patient-elicited niche open.

history.release_date: Founded 2018 (Pittsburgh, PA) by Shivdev Rao and Sandeep Konam; commercial ambient documentation launched from 2018, with early focus on evidence-based generative AI for clinical documentation.
history.key_milestones: 2019 $5M seed; 2020 $10M Series A; 2023 Series B; Feb 2024 Abridge Inside for Epic and $150M Series C at ~$850M; Feb 2025 $250M Series D at $2.75B and peer-reviewed Sutter Health JAMA Network Open study on clinician wellbeing; Jun 2025 $300M Series E at $5.3B led by a16z and expansion into inpatient/outpatient order workflows via Epic Workshop; Nov 2025 nursing documentation product at Reid Health; Feb 2026 KLAS #1 ambient AI and UCHealth systemwide expansion; Apr 2026 $316M Series E extension at $5.3B and clinical decision support partnership with Wolters Kluwer UpToDate; Jun 2026 AI-native clinician intelligence platform, NVIDIA Nemotron-based clinical foundation model, Eli Lilly equity investment and Northwestern Medicine enterprise rollout; Aug 2026 enterprise-wide CDS provisioning across 300+ systems.
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: The last six months were Abridge's most aggressive expansion to date. April 2026: closed a reported $316M Series E extension at the same $5.3B valuation and launched clinical decision support integrated with Wolters Kluwer UpToDate. June 2026: at its New York keynote it unveiled the first 'AI-native clinician intelligence platform' spanning pre-visit, intra-visit and post-visit workflows; announced a clinical foundation model co-developed with NVIDIA on the Nemotron family trained on Blackwell; took a strategic equity investment from Eli Lilly; and announced a system-wide enterprise implementation at Northwestern Medicine plus nursing integrations. July 2026: Sutter Health clinicians reached five million notes; Abridge published its Northwestern Medicine multi-vendor evaluation story. August 2026: made the clinical intelligence agent available enterprise-wide to every clinician at partner systems (300+ systems, 250M+ patients), reported CDS monthly-active use above 50% of eligible clinicians with query volume tripling in two months, shipped pre-visit summaries and CME credits in its August release, and published an engineering post on rubric-based offline evaluation. Its 'Care Signals' agentic capture experience was also rolled out. These changes materially extend Abridge from a scribe into a pre-visit and coding/payer platform, and its pre-visit summaries are chart-derived rather than patient-elicited.

market_positioning.target_users: Clinicians (physicians, advanced practice providers, residents/fellows and nurses) and the health systems that buy, govern and integrate AI for them - including CMIOs, IT/security and procurement leaders. Payer and life-sciences organizations are newer target audiences for its expanding platform.
market_positioning.market_segment: Ambient clinical documentation / AI medical scribing, now broadening into an 'AI-native clinician intelligence platform' spanning clinical decision support, medical coding/CDI, and payer/life-sciences workflows.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: Abridge markets itself as the leading enterprise-grade AI platform for clinical conversations and, since June 2026, as 'the first AI-native clinician intelligence platform organized around the patient, built for clinicians, and designed to help health systems coordinate the clinical, financial, and evidence-based decisions that shape every moment of care' - preparing clinicians before the visit, supporting them during the conversation, and reducing administrative burden after care. It emphasizes trust signals including deep EHR integration, Linked Evidence provenance, 28+ languages, 50+ specialties, the 2025/2026 Best in KLAS award, and enterprise security/governance as an alternative to 'shadow AI'.
